'''''Canna flaccida''''', sometimes referred to as the '''bandanna of the Everglades''', is a species of the [[Canna (plant)|''Canna'']] genus, a member of the family [[Cannaceae]]. The species is indigenous to the wetlands of the south-central and south-eastern United States from [[Texas]] to [[South Carolina]]. It is also reportedly naturalized in [[India]], the [[Philippines]], [[Mexico]], [[Panama]], [[Cuba]], the [[Dominican Republic]], [[Peru]] and southern [[Brazil]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/furtherInformation.do?name_id=223885 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Canna flaccida'']</ref>

''Canna flaccida'' was a parent to many of the early-hybridised cannas originally known as orchid flowered cannas, but now correctly named as Italian Group cannas. It grows well as a [[water canna]]. Originally described by the early American explorer, [[William Bartram]], when he found these plants blooming near the rivers of coastal [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. The seed floats down the rivers and becomes easily established on shorelines. Introduced to England in 1788.<ref>Johnson's Gardeners Dictionary, 1856</ref>

''Canna flaccida'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{cvt|1.5|m}}. It is hardy to zone 10 and is frost tender. In the north latitudes it is in flower from August to October, and the seeds ripen in October. The flowers are [[hermaphrodite]].<ref>Cooke, Ian, 2001. The Gardener's Guide to Growing cannas, Timber Press. {{ISBN|0-88192-513-6}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
In the last three decades of the 20th century, ''Canna'' species have been categorised by two different [[taxonomists]], [[Paulus Johannes Maria Maas]] from [[the Netherlands]] and [[Nobuyuki Tanaka]] from [[Japan]]. In this case both agree that ''C. flaccida'' is a distinct species, and the DNA work by [[Prince and Kress]] at the [[Smithsonian Institution]] confirms its uniqueness.<ref>Tanaka, N. 2001. Taxonomic revision of the family Cannaceae in the New World and Asia. Makinoa ser. 2, 1:34–43.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.botany2001.org/section12/abstracts/111.shtml |title=PRINCE, LINDA M.* and W. JOHN KRESS. Smithsonian Institution, NMNH - Botany, MRC-166, Washington, DC 20560-0166. - Species boundaries in Canna (Cannaceae): evidence from nuclear ITS DNA sequence data. |access-date=2006-09-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070312065416/http://www.botany2001.org/section12/abstracts/111.shtml |archive-date=2007-03-12 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Description==
''Canna flaccida'' is aquatic species, with narrow, blue-green (glaucous) leaves, very pretty, large, lightly perfumed, canary yellow flowers growing in clusters at the tops of long stalks. The lip of the flower is wavy. Flowers emerge in the evening and wither in the heat of the following day, the only member of the genus that behaves in this manner, all others open early in the morning and are strong enough to survive at least one day. It grows as a marginal plant in up to about {{cvt|15|cm}} of still or slow-moving water.<ref>{{eFloras|1|200028483|Canna flaccida |first1=W. John |last1=Kress |first2=Linda M. |last2=Prince}}</ref>
